card.name: Spoken-style clause starts in English prose
card.fires_on: Scattered words in informal, conversational English where a new clause or spoken-style sentence is about to start, such as a comma, colon, 'if', 'you' or 'they' after a break.

modes.label: Clause-joining words
modes.description: Words like 'if', 'you' or 'they' that open a new clause right after a dash, colon or comma.
modes.example: So -<< if>> the information is my lunch plans for tomorrow

modes.label: Punctuation ending a short phrase
modes.description: A comma or period after a short colloquial phrase, before the next phrase starts.
modes.example: They cry<<,>> but you don't see them cry,"

modes.label: Casual story or quote nouns
modes.description: Nouns like 'year' or 'store' in anecdotal or quoted speech.
modes.example: One<< year>> I even ended up in Mr. Williamson

card.writes: It pushes Chinese colloquial openers like 人家, 你看 and 怎么, and suppresses formal written phrases, so it favors a casual spoken tone.
card.plain: It fires at points in chatty English where a new spoken-style clause is about to begin.
